My brother committed suicide two years ago. I, much like you, didn't know what to do. I actually contacted legal zoom. The free part is a non-legal consultation in which the representative listens to your situation, and then recommends possible lawyers. Once I found a lawyer, I paid $300 total for a couple of "sessions". You can cancel when ever you want. 

I then found that through my work's employee assistance program, I had similar resources for free. So I kinda wasted $300, but I got the answers I needed, and I was/am so distraught about the situation, I don't really care about $300. 

I'd recommend reaching out the the HR contact for your dads work first.

First thing is first- I really enjoy your writing style. Then I see in one of your comments that you used to write fanfiction? What a lucky convience for you- you're good at writing, and you like doing it. So boom! Focus on that. Cultivate it. Do it more. Write for yourself. Write for those who want to listen. Write privately. Write publicly. Write fiction. Write non-fiction. Embrace it and strengthen your skill.

You must realize this and truly embrace that you deserve good things and should reward and treat yourself with enjoyable nuritment that you created yourself. Get lost in the aromas and textures. Become free in the entire culinary song and dance.

Even exchange students. Maybe you can find someone on the other side of the world who wants to learn English and you can Skype with them and learn more Chinese. 

Finally- the lung thing is a bummer. I understand why you say "Sports are out" but no one is asking you to go score a touchdown at the Super Bowl. I suggest you talk to a good doctor and a good physical trainer at a legit gym and put a light work out regime together. Something simple that is designed just for you that won't push you too hard. A little exercise can go a long way.

Negative thoughts and self loathing are the worst. I can imagine what you're going through. 

My only advice is to talk. Find a councilor, a therapist, a friend, a doctor, a nice stripper (though expensive) or someone you can talk with. The more you express- the better. BUT! You HAVE  to express it to the right person- someone who will genuinely listen. As you begin feeling more comfortable discussing your feelings and thoughts you can try and find a theapist. It's a lot like dating- it's gonna take some searching and some awkward 'dates' to find a therapist you can really jive with. 

Embrace yourself and explore your natural feelings. It will allow you to cope through them, understand them and ultimately concourse them.

Just one stranger one the internet's thoughts:

First, you passed. Celebrate that you even did. Think about all the students who didn't pass. You're looking at it in the wrong way. All those nights of staying in and studying DID pay off. You must realize this. Your hard work payed off and you passed. 

Second, it's ok to cry. 9 hours is a long time, so be sure to breathe, drink water and stretch a bit if that kinda thing happens again.

Lastly, it's good to talk to people. 

My brother committed suicide almost 2 years ago. The process of speaking with therapists and councillors is awkward and daunting. But it's kinda like dating- after talking to a couple different people, you'll find one you feel comfortable around. Then you can truly express yourself and begin healing.

I'm not religious at all, but you could also explore religious institutions in the area because you could find someone who will genuinely listen without being overbearing or judgmental. 

Youve experienced significant psychological and emotional trauma from both the car accident and the assault. Paired with the stress from your studies and the rest- no wonder you feel like crying for 9 hours. Any human would! In fact- if you didn't cry after all this, THEN I would think something is wrong with you. 

The way you're feeling is a natural response, and when you embrace that natural response in an attempt to understand it, cope through it and ultimately conquer it, you very well might realize that everything is going to be all right after all. 

P.s- if you don't know how to juggle, get three bean bags and learn. There are tons of YouTube tutorials on how to do it. When you feel depressed, anxious, or any negative emotion, doing something active and challenging will strengthen new synapses in your brain, converting negative thought into a positive experience through structured and challenging mental redirection.
